title: How the Hidden Singhs Were Sustained

blocks.text: The nawab boasts that the villages linked to the Singhs have been ravaged, their kin dragged out of hiding, and Mughal parties sent everywhere to strike them down. On the surface, the regime appears to have cut every ordinary path of livelihood and reduced the fugitives to hunger and disguise.

Yet the hidden Singhs were still being fed, and that stubborn fact unsettles the court. The page turns on the contradiction between relentless persecution and the continued survival of men who should, by the nawab's reasoning, have already perished from want.

A malicious informer then reveals the answer: local Sikhs and sympathizers feed themselves only after feeding the Khalsa, willingly accepting privation so that the hunted Singhs can keep moving. The regime's military pressure has therefore failed to break the moral economy that sustains the Panth.
